items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 1
description: "A Tale About Lies and How Swiftly They Spread Across the Earth"

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 2: Titus and Father Meager
description: "Suppose you sold me a young mare and suppose I brought it from you."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 3
description: "If it is done honestly and in God's way, then, I suppose, commerce is a godly business."

items.title: A Tale About Lies,  page 4: The Church of Nicholas the Sinner
description: "Let the mare remain here, while I fetch my money."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 5
description: "Ermil was sitting on a plank above them, dangling beneath the roof as he whitewashed the walls of the church Nicholas the Sinner."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 6: Ermil and the mare
description: "The mare jerked and, out of fear, bolted, and carried Ermil out of the yard and into the village street."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 7: Ermil, the mare, and Baba
description: "For the mare happened by Ermil's own hut just as his Baba emerged from the gate."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 8: Baba, Ermil, and the mare
description: "Ermil, unfortunately, hit his head on the roof of the shed and fell off the mare and lay in the yard motionless."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 9: Ermil and Baba
description: "But because of the blow he had suffered, something in Ermil's head had changed and there he lay, eyes blinking, looking at his wife and not saying a word."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 10
description: "On the one hand, she pitied Ermil, but on the other, she was desperate to find out what had happened."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 11: Ermil and Baba
description: "Three times in the night she turned and whispered to her husband with the same questions, but Ermil's answer was always the same: 'I don't have any idea, I don't have a clue.'"

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 12: Titus
description: "The red-haired Titus returned with his money."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 13
description: "I command you, Titus, go pick up the mare."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 14: Titus and Father Meager
description: "They went to investigate -- but there was no mare."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 15: Father Meager and Titus
description: "'You took my mare,' Father Meager yelled. 'And now you demand your money back?!'"

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 16
description: "The sky turned pitch dark, but they remained by the church arguing."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 17: Father Meager and Titus
description: "We will ask that man who was whitewashing the church where the mare went... he was here, perhaps he saw something... let him tell us!"

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 18
description: "But Ermil's Baba thought out a plan."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 19: Ermil and Baba
description: "Baba positioned herself behind Ermil, aimed well and hit him square on the back of his head -- on the very same spot Ermil had bumped on the roof of the shed."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 20
description: "Ermil was surprised. 'What mare are you talking about?'"

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 21
description: "'I know nothing about that!' replied his wife. 'The mare stands tied in my shed -- how can anyone sell it but me?'"

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 22: Ermil, Baba, and the mare
description: "They had not walked more than a few steps when she aimed well and hit Ermil square on the back of his head."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 23: Ermil
description: "'I don't have any idea. I don't have a clue.'"

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 24
description: "Ermil arrived at the church where the priest and the red-haired Titus were waiting for him."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 25: Titus and Father Meager
description: "Ermil's Baba instituted her own custom: hitting her husband on the back of his head every morning before he left for work and again when he returned in the evening."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 26: Father Meager
description: "Only Ermil's wife enjoyed life, as she waited for the foal to arrive."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 27
description: "The little fire inside was gleaming as Titus peered in and saw Ermil's Baba performing her custom over her husband's head."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 28: Baba, Ermil, and Titus
description: "'What kind of mare is he talking about?' thought Titus.

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 29: Titus
description: "And so Titus returned to his hut and sat down and started thinking."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 30
description: "He walked under Ermil's windows and peered in, examining everything down to the smallest detail."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 31: Titus
description: "No sooner had Ermil returned from work and sat down to eat his supper than his wife -- according to instituted custom -- smacked Ermil back into his smart mode and Titus walked in the door."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 32: Baba
description: "When Baba saw the red-haired Titus and heard Ermil's words, she began to tremble all over."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 33
description: "But Baba's fears were in vain. The red-haired Titus did not let Ermil speak."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 34: Ermil and Titus
description: "As the red-haired Titus spoke this way, he was nearly in tears, and kept moving closer and closer to Ermil."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 35
description: "The red-haired Titus began to kiss and to hug Ermil in all kinds of ways."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 36
description: "Baba was astonished that the visit had gone so well."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 37: The mare
description: "In the morning, she woke cheerful, humming to herself."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 38: Titus and Father Meager
description: "Baba had no idea what kind of trouble awaited her because of Titus' visit."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 39
description: "The red-haired Titus had enough and refused to speak with Baba any longer -- he walked straight into the shed and the others followed."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 40: Titus, Father Meager, Ermil, Baba, and the mare
description: "She grabbed onto the mare's tail and refused to let go."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 41: Father Meager and Titus
description: "They led the mare through the street, with Baba rocking on the tail."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 42
description: "'Wait a minute,' said the priest. 'I sold you the mare without a foal -- that was one price.'"

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 43
description: "Ermil finished whitewashing the church of Nicholas the Sinner; the mare had long since brought forth a foal; but they continued to argue."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 44
description: "The mare, in the meantime, brought forth yet another foal."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 45
description: "They spent everything they had, till the last kopeck -- until there was nothing left to keep the horses."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 46
description: "So, they started accepting donations. Whoever made a donation was permitted to join the argument."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 47
description: "The herd grows bigger, and so does the crowd."

items.title: A Tale About Lies, page 48
description: "One would assume that, for as long as there is space on this earth, the end is not in sight."
